name: Sennacherib
description: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Sennacherib king of Assyria comes up against the fenced cities of Judah and takes them.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

points: After these acts of faithfulness Sennacherib king of Assyria enters Judah and encamps against the fenced cities, thinking to win them for himself.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: Sennacherib sends servants to Jerusalem asking on what the people trust that they abide in the siege, and claims Hezekiah is persuading them to die by famine and thirst.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 32: Assyria Defeated and Hezekiah's End

points: In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod, sent by Sargon the king of Assyria, and fought against Ashdod and took it, the Most High spoke by Isaiah the son of Amoz.

note.label: Isaiah 20: Naked and Barefoot for a Sign

points: Sennacherib king of Assyria took Judah's defenced cities and sent Rabshakeh to mock Hezekiah in the Jews' language, boasting that no god of any nation had delivered his land out of the king of Assyria's hand.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the defended cities of Judah and took them. Assyria was the rod the Most High used to press Judah.
Sennacherib mocked the God of Hezekiah, and one angel slew 185,000 Assyrians in the night. Judah was saved without bow or sword, as Hosea said.
Tobit of Naphtali, carried captive to Nineveh, gave alms and buried his brethren whom Sennacherib killed in his rage after fleeing Judea.
